method: Read-only PDF, source-revision and dependency-lock comparison
question: Can the Task 09 stack be installed unchanged beside the accepted G1 stack?
finding: No. Accepted mjlab commit 8ee51fbc uses the compatible Torch 2.8 / MuJoCo 3.11 stack; sibling HEAD requires newer Torch. WBC's NumPy <2.5 constraint conflicts with the accepted NumPy 2.5.3 lock. Native MuJoCo preview and a separately pinned physics environment avoid changing robust_sav.

method: Hash-verified raw DuoBox loading and parent-composed forward kinematics
question: What do the recorded rotations mean, and can all four complete body motions be reconstructed?
finding: Selected actor ma, 21-joint hierarchy and inherited 120 Hz convention. Child rotations are parent-relative; treating them as world rotations causes 1.64–1.76 m errors. Correct composition reconstructs all four crops within 3.281e-7 m. Crop labels remain machine-selected candidates, not independently certified ground truth.

method: Procedural segmented triangle mesh and native MuJoCo kinematic replay
question: Can the four recorded punches be shown on a complete human without unavailable SMPL-X body files?
finding: The procedural DuoBox-aligned body supplied a reproducible visual preview without body-model weights. The first detailed appearance was rejected as unnecessarily realistic and archived. This was prescribed FK playback with no active physics or learning.

method: Featureless light-blue procedural mesh and CPU OSMesa rendering
question: Can the body be visually simple while preserving the recorded motions?
finding: Removed face, hair, clothing detail and separate visible toes. Neutral compiled mesh height was 1.800000 m; 29 mesh assets, 9,562 vertices and 19,008 triangles. Four videos decoded successfully; FK errors were at most 3.61e-7 m. No actuators, gravity or collision participation were enabled.

method: Full orientation and rigid-transform audit over 855 poses and synthetic wrist-axis rotations
question: Were glove rotations being lost at the wrist?
finding: No transform bug was found. Hand/source disagreement was 3.88e-12 degrees and hand-relative glove orientation drift 3.1e-14 degrees. Flattened gloves and pale orientation patches made the existing rotation visible. Left blue/right red colors were historical review aids, not the later production perception contract.

method: Allocated Slurm V100 probe and native NVIDIA EGL rendering
question: Which GPUs are exposed on this server and can the project render on one?
finding: The exposed partition was xeon-g6-volta with Tesla V100-PCIE-32GB; mit_normal_gpu/L40S was not exposed. Python 3.12.3, MuJoCo 3.11.0 and a valid 64x64 NVIDIA EGL image passed. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES contained a UUID, requiring allocation-aware EGL device resolution.

method: CPU retargeting and native MuJoCo NVIDIA EGL rendering on one V100
question: Can one allocated GPU render all four previews reproducibly?
finding: All four previews completed; application time 15.67 s and batch time 23 s. CUDA-to-EGL PCI device matching passed. This validates GPU rendering of kinematic replay, not GPU physics or learning.

method: Four independent one-GPU Slurm array tasks across two nodes
question: Does device selection remain correct when concurrent jobs receive different physical GPUs?
finding: All four tasks passed. Each process used CUDA logical device 0, but two required EGL device index 1. Device UUID/PCI matching prevented accidental rendering on the wrong GPU. Four GPUs were tested, not eight-GPU distributed training; all eight single-job/array videos decoded and trajectories matched CPU references to 1e-12.

method: Smooth path deformation, active-arm Jacobian IK, native MuJoCo FK and GPU EGL rendering
question: Can the four punches be redirected toward a fixed G1 head without machine learning?
finding: All four near-contact previews reached their anchors with 0.265–0.408 mm IK error. Visible-head separation bounds stayed positive at 2.967–5.934 mm. G1 coordinates were fixed in all 855 poses. The approximately 0.184 m glove/head center distances did not meet the later audited 0.14 m contact contract; these were visual near-contact results.

method: Page-33 and Task 08 source audit; explicit both-glove geometry utilities
question: Do 0.14 m contact and 0.16 m safe clearance transfer to an articulated human?
finding: Yes. Use attached glove centers, 0.08 m gloves and the actual 0.06 m head proxy. Either glove at distance <=0.14 m is contact; both >=0.16 m gives safe glove clearance; the band between is unsafe without contact. Both hands remain hazards in all phases. No robust_sav threshold change was needed, and analytic contact does not imply impact impulses.

method: Literature/model comparison and engineering rigid-body design
question: Is a detailed human mesh or muscle simulation necessary for physical punching?
finding: A simple articulated body with masses/inertias, constraints, bounded effort and floor contact is sufficient for a pilot. Adopted an intermediate 75 kg DuoBox-derived body with 20 ball joints/60 motors and a free root to isolate controller issues. Its extra elbow/knee freedom, disabled self-collision and uncalibrated mass/strength remain limitations. The proposed 34-scalar-DOF alternative was not implemented.

method: Kinematic arm IK toward a 0.135 m center target, with frozen head and approach-yaw variants
question: Can the four families actually enter the unchanged Task 08 contact envelope?
finding: All 12 references (four families x -6/0/+6 degree approach yaw) had sampled contact and finite states. Base minima were jab 0.135798 m, cross 0.135854 m, left hook 0.134628 m and right hook 0.134932 m. Combined-scene FK agreed within 1e-10 m. This is geometric acceptance, not balanced physical execution or validated launch TTC.

method: Torch optimization, Warp kernel, batched mjlab dynamics and camera probe
question: Does the accepted pinned training stack execute on the available V100?
finding: Torch's five finite-gradient Adam steps reduced loss from 1.0700 to 0.9883, and batched floor physics/camera stages ran. Overall probe failed because diagnostic metadata used obsolete wp.context after the numerical Warp operation. This was an API bookkeeping failure, not evidence that V100 physics was unsupported.

method: Public Warp toolkit accessor and repeated GPU probe
question: Does replacing the obsolete Warp accessor complete the numerical runtime checks?
finding: The structured probe passed after using wp.get_cuda_toolkit_version(). Subsequent visual review found red/blue channels reversed in diagnostic unpacking. Corrected packed RGB extraction and a red-object assertion were required before treating camera colors as validated.

method: Native CPU MuJoCo integration with bounded quaternion pose-PD and GPU EGL rendering
question: Will a statically conditioned guard and pose-PD alone support the human?
finding: No. Standing and jab fell despite a free unactuated root and bounded effort. Jab maximum sole drift was 0.238997 m; the standing pelvis reached 0.080265 m from an initial 0.986150 m. This motivated contact-aware inverse statics and balance feedback rather than pose playback or hidden root assistance.

method: Actual MuJoCo-Warp integration and raycast cameras through pinned mjlab; corrected RGB unpacking
question: Do training math, dynamics, physical motor transmission and Task 08 camera geometry work together?
finding: Passed five Torch updates, a 512-element Warp kernel, 16 settling sphere worlds, human/G1 RGB-depth-ID rendering, and four physical-human worlds with torque response. Task 08 camera geometry was verified. Near-contact glove occlusion was 93.0%, median depth 0.0204 m and only 4.76% of pixels in the accepted 0.1–3 m range; perception/policy performance remains unvalidated.

method: Native CPU MuJoCo physics with quaternion PD, planted-support conditioning and contact-aware balance feedforward
question: Does adding support-aware torque computation resolve the initial falls across all families?
finding: Jab and cross remained upright with 8.43 mm and 26.10 mm maximum sole drift. Left hook remained upright but slipped 0.253 m; right hook fell with 3.37 m drift. These initial records did not yet include the later explicit contact gate. The controller helped but did not establish a four-family physical solution.

method: Native CPU MuJoCo physics, support-conditioned/re-aimed reference and 0.6x source playback
question: Does slowing the motion improve executed contact and support?
finding: Jab contacted at 0.138893 m with 3.63 mm drift. Cross missed at 0.203737 m; left hook missed at 0.339482 m with 59.39 mm drift; right hook fell. The conditioned jab became the first matched native/Warp controller input.

method: Native MuJoCo kinematic playback and NVIDIA EGL rendering on allocated V100
question: Do the contacting reference paths render correctly beside G1?
finding: Four contact-directed base references rendered and all videos fully decoded; job completed in 15 s. Videos deliberately retain kinematic lower-body motion and visible hovering. A GPU rendering job does not make these dynamically supported trajectories.

method: Actual GPU MuJoCo-Warp physics with a synchronous CPU quaternion controller writing only bounded torques
question: Does the successful slow jab execute on the pinned GPU physics backend without pose overwrite?
finding: At 0.6x speed, Warp jab minimum distance was 0.138935 m, maximum foot drift 3.65 mm and double support 99.84%. Native comparison contacted at 0.138893 m. Maximum root-position backend difference was 0.118 mm. Five-second standing also passed. No root actuator force or state overwrite after reset; not a high-throughput GPU-resident controller.

method: Matched native and actual GPU MuJoCo-Warp physics at source playback speed
question: Does the same slow-jab controller also hit at full source speed?
finding: Both backends remained upright and torque-bounded, but the punch missed at 0.162581 m; foot drift rose to 8.80 mm and torque reached its norm cap. The recorded control status passed while contact_goal_achieved was false. Tracking, not backend compatibility, limited this attempt.

method: Native CPU MuJoCo physics; smoothed/re-aimed planted references, 0.3x speed and gain scale 1.5
question: Can difficult families pass contact and support after conditioning and slowing?
finding: Cross contacted at 0.137540 m with 7.80 mm maximum sole drift; left hook at 0.116591 m with 5.50 mm drift. Both passed isolated-punch/support gates with unchanged effort limits. These are slowed deterministic cases, not full-speed or cross-family generalization.

method: Native CPU MuJoCo physics; four-frame Gaussian smoothing, 0.10 m reference aiming and gain scale 1.5
question: Can reference/controller changes recover contact at source speed without increasing strength?
finding: Yes for one jab. Executed minimum center distance was 0.112658 m; first interpolated contact 0.801475 s from cycle start; sole drift 5.05 mm; double support 99.786%. Torque-vector limits were unchanged and root assistance absent. G1 was fixed and head events analytic, without impact response.

method: Native CPU MuJoCo physical tracking at 5 ms, 0.6x reference speed and reduced gain scale 0.6
question: Can the human controller run at the accepted G1 plant's 5 ms timestep?
finding: This lower-gain 5 ms attempt fell, with 1.014 m sole drift and a 0.159821 m miss. Earlier 5 ms divergence and this retest leave a real timing gap: demonstrated old-body tracking uses 2 ms physics, while shared-plant integration requires an explicit clock decision and G1 revalidation.

method: Immutable boundary-only reference player and dimensional endpoint-to-start state comparisons
question: Can the geometrically contacting clips simply be concatenated into continuous punches?
finding: No. All 16 base-family endpoint-to-start pairs failed guard admission, including same-family repeats. Jab-to-jab root mismatch was 42.85 mm and maximum joint-speed mismatch 3.88956 rad/s. The adapter freezes launch plans and rejects mid-cycle reselection; reference completion enters waiting_guard instead of teleporting or launching automatically.

method: Native CPU MuJoCo physics; two 0.6x jabs, target bridges and measured guard admission with one reset
question: Can a physical human recover and launch a second jab without resetting its state?
finding: Two jabs completed over 9.79 s / 4,895 physics steps. Contact minima were 0.110467 and 0.110762 m; sole drift 6.698 mm; double support 99.9796%; no saturation or root/external force. Second launch at 4.898 s followed at least 0.10 s measured guard dwell. No intermediate state overwrites; only one deterministic same-family sequence was validated.

method: Native CPU MuJoCo physics; 12 cm forward stance offset, deeper aim, 0.3x speed and gain scale 3
question: Was the remaining right-hook failure an unreachable reference or an executed tracking deficit?
finding: Earlier references already contacted but the executed glove lagged, implicating shoulder tracking and post-IK derivative spikes. Revised stance/aim and gains produced 0.113157 m contact with 5.13 mm sole drift, unchanged effort caps and passed support/contact gates. This differs from the gain/conditioning used for the other families.

method: Actual GPU MuJoCo-Warp integration with CPU bounded-torque feedback, matched against native MuJoCo
question: Does the improved full-speed native jab transfer to actual GPU physics beside fixed G1?
finding: Warp contact distance was 0.112658289 m, first contact 0.801474686 s, sole drift 5.05448 mm and double support 99.7859%. Root actuation was zero. Native/Warp maximum root-position difference was 0.686 micrometres for this nominal rollout. Contact was sampled every 2 ms; no impact response or robustness guarantee follows.

method: Independent final-reference/executed-FK audits, full video decoding and regression checks
question: Are the accepted old-body physical demonstrations and their evidence internally consistent?
finding: Four isolated family cases plus the continuous two-jab case were collected with exact source jobs and speed factors. All five review videos fully decoded; final reference/executed cone audits passed recorded tolerances. Historical suite reported 71 tests plus 4 subtests and Ruff passing. The gallery uses native CPU physics and GPU rendering, distinct from the separate Warp comparison.

method: Original Task 09 PDF reconciliation, model survey and measured-gap assessment
question: Should the diagnostic ball-joint mannequin become the final learned adversary body?
finding: The original plan already named SMPL-X/SMPLSim primary and SOMA23 fallback. Its broad default articulation still required constraints, force accounting and retargeting. The existing 20-ball rig remained a useful classical baseline, not a validated anatomical training body. The recommended next milestone was a constrained scalar body, complete jab reference and learned physical imitation; detailed skin, muscles and a full framework stack were unnecessary.
